captions.detailed: A matte black gravel bicycle steering assembly featuring a carbon fork with tapered, straight blades and a wide crown. It is connected via a tapered threadless steerer tube to a prominent four-bolt ahead stem. Clamped in the faceplate of the stem are flared, drop-style gravel handlebars. The entire assembly is designed to rotate as a single unit around the steerer tube's axis to simulate natural steering motion.
captions.instruction: Create a 3D model of a gravel bike carbon fork and steering assembly. The model should include a dual-blade carbon fork with a tapered crown, a threadless steerer tube, a four-bolt ahead-style stem, and flared drop handlebars clamped at the center faceplate, finished in a uniform matte black material.
captions.factory: The code constructs an ArticulatedObject containing the steering assembly. It starts by modeling the fork blades using tapered extrusions or lofted shapes, joined to a custom-profiled crown. A cylindrical steerer tube is extruded vertically from the crown. The stem is constructed using a series of box and cylinder primitives combined with boolean operations to form the clamping body, faceplate, and hardware recesses. The flared drop handlebars are generated by sweeping a circular profile along a 3D spline path representing the tops, ramps, and flared drops. All components are grouped into a single rigid part, or articulated with a revolute joint representing the steering axis.
